- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after spikes), especially in early forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive or when recent history shows mean reversion.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts in the 10–20 day horizon if sentiment has recently turned negative.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if true price drops after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative and price is rising, reduce forecast by 5–15% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- Forecast should not exceed 2–3 standard deviations above recent 18-day mean unless sentiment is strongly bullish and recent price is trending up.
- In 30-day horizon, if sentiment is negative and price is trending down, reduce forecast by 10–20% to avoid overestimating recovery.
